chunks: And it is narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn Khālid, who said:
I said to Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, “May I be your ransom,”
regarding the people’s saying: “The guarantor is liable.”
So he عليه السلام said: “There is no liability upon the guarantor; liability is only upon the one who consumed the wealth.”

key_terms.أَكَلَ: consumed or took for personal use
key_terms.الضَّامِنُ: the guarantor, the one who undertakes a guarantee
key_terms.الْمَالَ: the property or wealth in question
key_terms.غُرْمٌ: financial liability or loss to be borne

ai.seo_question: Is the guarantor financially liable in Shia hadith, or is liability on the one who used the wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning guarantee and financial liability. Imam Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام states that mere guarantee does not itself place the financial loss upon the guarantor; rather, liability rests on the one who actually consumed the property.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3402 - It is narrated from Al-Husayn ibn Khalid who said:
I said to Abu al-Hasan (as), "May I be your ransom!

People say, 'The guarantor (al-damin) is liable (gharim).'"
Imam (as) replied: "There is no liability (ghurm) upon the guarantor.
The liability is upon the one who consumed the wealth."
